stories.headline: Houthi escalation in Yemen threatens Red Sea shipping and Saudi infrastructure

sources.body: Yemen's Houthis on Monday said they fired dozens of drones and ballistic missiles at military targets in Saudi Arabia as the rebels stepped up attacks on Saudi infrastructure while advancing along Yemen's Red Sea coast towards ​the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
sources.headline: Mideast live: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted military facilities in Saudi Arabia

sources.body:
Yemeni government forces have advanced in western Taiz after successfully repelling a Houthi offensive.

Armed forces affiliated with Yemen’s internationally recognised government have retaken positions from the Houthis and are advancing in the southwestern Taiz province as clashes intensify.

Reporting from Taiz on Monday, Al Jazeera Arabic’s Yasser Hassan said forces loyal to the Saudi Arabia-backed Yemeni government advanced in western Taiz on Sunday after successfully repelling a Houthi offensive.

“This comes with the support of air strikes targeting Houthi gatherings. The air force continues to bomb the Houthis. On the west coast in Mocha, Dhubab, and their surroundings,” Hassan said, citing a source in government forces.

In a statement on Monday, the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (supporters of God), said they launched attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia using dozens of ballistic missiles and drones.

The group said the attacks targeted “military facilities and infrastructure, including aircraft hangars, radar installations, runways, ammunition depots and other targets at King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait”, Saudi Arabia.

It said the attacks were a response to a Saudi offensive, which involved more than 300 air strikes across Yemen over five days.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi Arabia on the Houthi claims.

On Sunday, the Saudi civil defence agency sent alerts for the city of Abha and the region around Khamis Mushait, but they were quickly lifted shortly afterwards.

Fighting in Yemen’s more than 10-year civil war reignited in July, threatening a United Nations-brokered truce that halted large-scale violence in 2022, after the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.

The fighting soon spilled over beyond the country’s borders, with the Houthis carrying out air attacks on southern Saudi Arabia, including oil facilities. Dozens of people were wounded in those attacks.

Clashes in Yemen intensified last week after the Houthis captured parts of the country’s Red Sea coast, fortifying their hold on the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a key waterway which handles about 12 percent of global trade, including 11 percent of maritime oil and 8 percent of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The waterway has been an economic lifeline for Saudi Arabia and its oil exports, as the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively blocked by Iranian forces since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in February.

The Houthis captured more strategic islands in the southern Red Sea, The Associated Press news agency reported on Monday, citing Yemeni government and Houthi officials.

Houthi fighters were deployed on the islands of Greater Hanish and Lesser Hanish about 86 nautical miles (160km) north of the Bab al-Mandeb, according to two government officials and a Houthi official, the AP reported.

Meanwhile, the International Organization for Migration said on Sunday the fighting in Yemen in recent weeks had displaced nearly 86,000 people.
sources.headline: Yemen gov’t forces advance in Taiz as Houthis claim attack on Saudi Arabia

sources.body:
Iran-allied Houthis say drones and missiles used in attack that targeted ‘weapons depots and command and control centres’ in southern Saudi Arabia

Houthi fighters have said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia , as Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government described the rebels’ swift advance along the Red Sea coast as a “painful” development in a new front in the Iran war.

The UN said on Sunday that nearly 86,000 people had fled Yemen , most of them since early September when the Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched a large-scale offensive that last week resulted in the capture of a key port city and an island on the Bab al-Mandab strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the strait of Hormuz.

The overnight attack at the southern Sharurah base targeted “weapons depots and command and control centres that are managing the aggression against our nation and people”, the Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree wrote on X. The date of the operation was not specified.

The Saudi civil defence force said a projectile had fallen in al-Tawwal governorate near the border with Yemen along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. The statement blamed the Houthis . It also said sirens had sounded in Sharurah governorate but no damage was reported.

Yemeni government forces said they had struck Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha and later attacked other Houthi positions in the south-west of the country.

“Air force of the armed forces targeted positions and barracks of the terrorist Houthi group with three airstrikes” in the Taiz region, the Yemeni military said on Sunday.

A senior government official in Yemen said its forces would return to the Red Sea coast and fight back, after people fleeing the Houthi advance told the Associated Press they had seen forces withdrawing and urging people to run.

Sultan al-Arada, a member of the ruling presidential council, described the collapse of government forces in Mocha and elsewhere on Yemen’s west coast as “painful and regrettable”.

Al-Arada, who is also the governor of Yemen’s central Marib province, said in a televised interview broadcast late on Saturday night that forces “are currently regrouping and will return to the battle in one form or another”. The renewed fighting in Yemen has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.

The US news site Axios reported that the Saudi crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, twice called Donald Trump to request strikes on the Houthis last week, but that the request was rejected. Trump acknowledged the conversation on Saturday but did not say whether Washington would take any action. “Everything’s gonna work out fine and dandy,” he told reporters.

The clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the sea’s southern entrance.

The waterway has become an important artery for Saudi oil exports after Iran largely cut off shipments through the Gulf with its blockade on the strait of Hormuz in response to the US-Israeli assault on the country.
sources.headline: Houthis claim attack on Saudi base as fighting flares with Yemeni forces

stories.headline: Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline

sources.body:
Price spike comes as rebel Houthis in Yemen target oil infrastructure and capture strategic island in Bab al-Mandab strait

Oil prices have climbed above $108 a barrel after a series of drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to close its east-west crude pipeline.

Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil prices, surged to as much as $108.03 a barrel on Monday – a 3.25% increase on the day.

The spike came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi forces launched several attacks against Saudi Arabia and captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday, expanding their control of the waterway.

Market concerns were also fuelled by the Gulf states postponing a meeting with Tehran to discuss creating a temporary shipping lane through the strait of Hormuz, a vital channel through which a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supply normally passes.

Traders in the kingdom have warned it will run out of oil stocks for export if it does not reopen the east-west pipeline within days.

Gas prices also climbed higher on Monday, with the UK benchmark rising by 5% to 208.73p a therm – its highest level since December 2022.

Energy prices have surged this year, as the US-Israel war with Iran has disrupted oil and gas supply across the Middle East. The oil price peaked at $126 in April but later fell back over the summer amid hopes of a lasting ceasefire.

The price then began to climb again after the memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran fell apart. After a fresh stepping up of hostilities the benchmark again rose above the $100 a barrel threshold last week for the first time since July.

Chris Beauchamp, of the broker IG, said that a “move back to the spring highs” looked increasingly likely.

“Oil markets are being subjected to their worst fears all at once – attacks on energy infrastructure, the closure of Hormuz and a breakdown in attempts to restart negotiations,” he said.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning

“The risk of further disruption is also spreading beyond the Gulf, with the threat of renewed Houthi attacks on shipping adding another layer of uncertainty around key energy and trade routes.

“The major surprise is how calm markets remain in the face of all this, but if prices breach the March highs, things could get ugly very quickly.”

Oil output from Saudi Arabia had been under pressure before the attacks on its major pipeline. Riyadh told the Opec oil cartel recently that its crude production in August was at its lowest level since 1990, according to Bloomberg.

The spike in energy prices has triggered higher inflation across large economies around the world. Central bankers in the US, Japan and the UK must contend with the renewed rise in the cost of energy and accelerating price rises as they prepare to set interest rates this week.
sources.headline: Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut down Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline

sources.body: The United States begins G20 meetings in Houston on Monday promoting “energy abundance” as President Donald Trump’s war against Iran disrupts global fuel markets. Delegations from major economies, including China, India, Japan and Germany, will attend alongside oil producers Canada and Saudi Arabia. Russia is also expected to participate.
sources.headline: US hosts G20 energy talks in Texas as Iran war disrupts global fuel markets

stories.headline: Iranian cargo ship struck near the Strait of Hormuz as regional talks are delayed

sources.body: An Iranian cargo vessel was struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, killing one person and wounding four, Iranian state media said. Tehran blamed a “terrorist enemy” for the attack, which came as threats to shipping intensified around the Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb straits.
sources.headline: Iranian cargo vessel struck near Qeshm Island as Oman delays Tehran-Gulf talks

stories.headline: Sweden’s centre-left bloc holds a razor-thin lead after the general election

sources.body: Sweden's centre-left opposition on ​Monday looked the most likely to form the next government as preliminary election results showed it holding a narrow three-seat lead over the right-wing ruling parties with most of the votes counted after Sunday's vote. Party leaders, however, have been cautious about claiming victory or accepting defeat with 353 election districts still to be counted ‌and overseas votes not likely to be tallied until Wednesday.
sources.headline: Centre-left holds narrow lead in knife-edge Sweden vote

sources.body:
Race too close to call and may take days to become clear despite early exit polls suggesting left bloc win

With most of the votes counted, Sweden’s national election remained too close to call on Sunday night, with left-wing parties holding a lead of just a single seat according to a partial tally by the election authority.

Earlier in the night, exit polls suggested that the country was on course for a brand new left-leaning government. But as the votes were counted, it was apparent it could take days for the outcome to become clear.

With 80% of votes counted, there was just one seat between the left and right blocs. The left-leaning opposition parties, led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson, had 175 and the rightwing parties, led by the Moderates prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, had 174.

At 10:30pm local time, broadcaster SVT predicted there were only 20,000 votes between the blocs.

The election authority said a preliminary vote count may not be ready until Thursday.

Kristersson, the incumbent prime minister, said the voters had had their say, but “we still don’t have a final result.”

“Which government will lead Sweden in the coming years is still an open question, and we will do everything we can to ensure that this government will be the very best for our country,” Kristersson told supporters.

The Social Democrats remain Sweden’s biggest party, but look to have had their worst result in decades. Speaking just before midnight local time, Andersson addressed supporters to say that every vote must be counted.

“We will have to wait for the final election results. But my message is clear: we Social Democrats will always be ready to take responsibility for the result. It seems like it will be very even,” she said.

“But right now we are leading. If it stands, then Sweden will have a new government. But we have to wait for the final result, so let me end where I began, in democracy, the finest thing we have.”

It was also a bad night for the far-right Sweden Democrats, who are hoping to enter government for the first time. They slipped from the country’s second biggest party to third.

The deputy prime minister, Ebba Busch, of the Christian Democrats, told her supporters that Sweden would be going “to bed with uncertainty” and may have to wait until Wednesday for a result. But she remained adamant that the ruling right-leaning coalition should remain in government.

“This is a very clear message for the only unified government alternative in this election campaign,” she said in an upbeat speech. “This will be a real nail-biter, this could be uncertain all the way until Wednesday.”

It comes after an unusually heated and polarised campaign punctuated by personal attacks between leaders, accusations of misinformation and Maga-inspired ads. Polls suggested an extremely tight race , with one showing just 0.3 percentage points between the left and right blocs.

Polling stations across the country opened at 8am local time (7am UK time). Enthusiasm among voters appeared to be high. A record 3.6 million voters took part in early voting and there were reports of long queues at some polling stations.
sources.headline: Swedish election: centre-left parties lead by just a single seat with most votes counted

sources.body:
Sweden’s opposition bloc is projected to win the election with a one-seat majority over the ruling coalition.

Sweden’s high-stakes general election results remain too close to call as vote counting continues, with early trends showing the centre-left opposition in a narrow lead over the right-wing government.

Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson told supporters on Sunday the opposition coalition is leading the count, and if the results stand, “Sweden will get a new government”.

Earlier, polling ended at 8pm local time (18:00 GMT). With 94.4 percent of votes counted, the centre-left opposition was expected to win 176 seats in the 349-member parliament, the Swedish Election Authority said in its latest update early on Monday, against 173 for the right-wing governing bloc.

However, Andersson’s party, which governed Sweden for most of the 20th century and remains the country’s largest, also looked to be heading for its worst score in more than a century with 28.1 percent of the vote, down 2.2 percentage points from 2022.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who leads the ruling coalition, said he would contact other party leaders after the results, adding that it remains an open question who will govern Sweden in the coming years.

“When we have the final result, it’s a good idea to look at possible combinations,” he said, adding that “there is a very clear non-socialist majority, or non-left-leaning economic majority in the Swedish parliament. And I will actually take note of that and at least figure out whether there are any possibilities.”

Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Akesson said “we will not know tonight” who will form the next government. The party took 17.6 percent, down almost 3 percentage points from its 2022 result of 20.5 percent, and fell to third place behind Kristersson’s Moderates.

Counting of late postal ballots and votes cast at Swedish embassies abroad begins on Wednesday, and the final result is not expected until the end of the week.

Earlier in the campaign, Sweden’s left-wing bloc appeared headed for a comfortable victory over Kristersson’s four-party alliance, which includes the nationalist Sweden Democrats. Polls early in the year had given the opposition bloc a lead of about 10 percentage points, but the race tightened steadily, and that advantage had collapsed to just two to three percentage points by the final weeks, turning what had looked like a relatively predictable election into a much closer contest.

A victory for Andersson would provide some respite for left-leaning parties across Europe, where right-wing and far-right parties have been gaining ground. Just last week, Alternative for Germany (AfD) won 44 percent of the vote in a key state election, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level in the country for the first time since World War II.

With roots in the neo-Nazi movement, the Sweden Democrats became the largest party on the right in 2022 and a crucial source of parliamentary support for Kristersson’s minority government.
sources.headline: Sweden’s centre-left leads by three seats as vote counting continues

stories.headline: Russia strikes a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine’s border with Poland

sources.body:
A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through.

No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said.

Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv.

Russia said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said that "quite possibly, the target of this drone could have been the diplomatic train".

Former CIA chief David Petraeus, who had been on board another train at Yahodyn station at the time of the strike, said the incident was "terrifying".

In an interview with the New York Times, Petraeus said: "This is the act of a truly barbaric leader trying to terrorize Ukrainian civilians."

In a statement, Ukrzaliznytsia said the diplomatic train "had left the station earlier than expected because of the timetable change... due to constant threats of Russian strikes".

It also said an evacuation order for passengers on the hit train had been given "just 15 minutes" before the strike by a Russian jet-propelled drone.

Both Ukrainian and Polish authorities said the Russian drone had struck 2km (1.2 miles) from the Polish border.

Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt, who had also attended the conference in Kyiv, told the BBC passengers on board his train had been told to prepare for evacuation before subsequently being allowed to continue their journey.

"On the train I was on we received order to prepare evacuation after it had stopped. But after a number of minutes we were informed that it was clear and we could proceed," he said.

That train then safely arrived at Poland's border station in Dorohusk.

Some reports have suggested Bildt was on the same train as Johnson, but the former UK prime minister has not confirmed any details.

Johnson wrote on X: "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning.

He said this was "the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day - even on civilian railways" and urged Kyiv's allies to urgently provide Ukrainians "the air defences they need".

Ukraine has made repeated pleas to its allies - particularly the US - to provide more interceptors to defend against daily Russian attacks that increasingly use fast-moving ballistic missiles and jet-propelled drones.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the "barbaric strikes" at the Ukraine-Poland border in Yahodyn amounted to "[Russian President Vladimir] Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and Nato" and renewed calls for more sanctions on Moscow.

"Putin needs to understand that his barbarism will be met with decisive action that increases the cost of war for him to an unacceptable level. This is the only way to stop him," he said.
sources.headline: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station

sources.body: Ukraine and Poland on Sunday condemned Russian strikes close to the Polish border as an "escalation" in the war, after drones struck a Warsaw-bound train. Ukraine's rail operator said former British PM Boris Johnson and ex-US CIA director David Petraeus were at a border train station nearby around the time the train was hit.
sources.headline: Ukraine, Poland condemn Russia after drone strikes train near border

stories.headline: Search expands for more than 120 people missing after a ferry capsizes in Indonesia’s Java Sea

sources.body: Indonesian rescue teams on Monday deployed specialised underwater teams and navy-operated underwater drones as the search for more than 120 people missing in the Virgo Transport 8 ferry capsizing intensified.
sources.headline: Indonesia intensifies search for more than 120 missing after ferry capsizes in Java Sea

sources.body:
Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continue

One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu , the country’s government says.

The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.

“Our hearts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones,” Vanuatu prime minister Jotham Napat’s office said in a statement on Sunday.

“Search and rescue operations are continuing.”

Fifteen of those onboard have been “accounted for alive” and one body has been recovered, the statement said.

“Over 30 people remain missing at sea,” it said.

“To the survivors, we ⁠pray for your strength and recovery. To the families of ​those ​missing and those we ​have lost, please know that the nation stands ​with you ‌in this time ​of ​grief.”

An investigation into potential negligence has been launched.

“This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel,” the statement added.

The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in New Caledonia said it was assisting with the search, and a French Armed Forces aircraft was deployed on Sunday morning.

The centre said 12 people were located on Sunday morning.

Matai Seremaiah, the member of parliament for Luganville who is assisting in the search, said efforts would concentrate on the south-east coast where currents may have carried survivors.
sources.headline: One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas

stories.headline: AI-linked stocks fall as industry leaders call for a slowdown in development

sources.body:
Shares in tech firms tumble across Asia with Nasdaq also likely to dip later after Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX leaders back call

AI-linked stocks tumbled on Monday after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX called for a slowdown in “reckless” development citing fears the technology could soon run out of control.

Shares in SoftBank, a Japanese investor that is a big backer of OpenAI, slumped 13%, while the South Korean Kospi stock index, which relies heavily on chip makers that supply AI companies, dropped by 3%.

Shares in the big global microchip supplier Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company dropped 1.2%. Futures for the Nasdaq pointed to a 1.3% drop in the tech-heavy index when the US stock market opens this afternoon.

In Europe, shares in the Dutch tech manufacturer ASML, Europe’s biggest company by value and an important supplier for the semiconductor industry, slumped by as much as 5.4% in morning trading.

There was, however, a rally in shares that have been threatened by the rise of AI, including the advertising group WPP, which rose by 3.1%, and the analytics business Relx, which rose 4.2%. The latter had suffered a sharp fall earlier this year after Anthropic launched a suite of new data and automation tools.

The market swings come after the chief executive of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, appealed for the AI industry to “slow down”.

He said that “building too fast is reckless”, warning that a swarm of AI agents could cause hundreds of billions of dollars of damage by “taking over the entire internet” in future.

Amodei’s claims have been disputed by some experts , but on Monday investors began to price in a slowdown that would make it harder for the industry to pay for hundreds of billions of dollar in investments in AI infrastructure.

The OpenAI CEO, Sam Altman, the Google DeepMind chief, Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX boss, Elon Musk, all posted support for Amodei’s essay on slowing AI development, titled “We Must Pace the Frontier”.

Altman added that he would match Amodei’s commitment to embedding outside evaluators within his company to verify safety practices.

Fears continue to grow over the rapid pace and lack of regulation in AI development. On Monday, a cross-party group of MPs and peers identified a series of human rights risks posed by AI , arguing that no country in the world has laws sufficient to contain them.

Meanwhile, China’s top intelligence official has warned that the use of AI by adversaries could pose a risk to the country’s political and social security.

Chen Yixin wrote in a government outlet on Sunday that advanced US models such as Anthropic’s Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber could pose serious risks to Beijing’s critical information ​infrastructure, and called for a comprehensive strengthening of AI security.

However, Donald Trump rejected the calls to pace AI development. The US president told reporters over the weekend: “We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins.”
sources.headline: AI-linked stocks fall after tech bosses call for slowdown in ‘reckless’ development

sources.body:
There has been no shortage of warnings from AI's top bosses about existential threats over the years.

I attended the world's first AI safety summit in Bletchley Park in November 2023 where the focus was on the most serious threats imaginable, posed by the most powerful AI models.

At the time, many thought this was in the realm of sci-fi and the real threats were comparatively far more mundane: job losses, cheating in exams. Three years later, many of those same voices don't seem to be so sure.

On Saturday head of AI company Anthropic, Dario Amodei, urged the pace of development to be slowed down - the bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk said they agreed with him.

Meanwhile AI researcher Jacob Coxon - who quit Anthropic - told the BBC on Sunday staff who were developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.

They all add up to a chorus of serious voices urging a slowdown, but although it might sound like a quick fix, it is far from an easy solution.

America is widely understood to be terrified of losing the race to build the most powerful AI to China.

On Sunday President Trump made his own views clear, claiming the US was ahead of China in the AI race and declaring: "Whoever wins AI, wins."

China isn't renowned for wanting to come second. Everyone I speak to says that even if their company pauses, others will not and they will just get left behind. It reminds me of the height of the campaign for nuclear disarmament. The problem then too was that nobody wanted to go first.

There is also the question of how on earth a slowdown would be enforced. Who would police it? Would we be relying on the AI companies to be transparent about what they are doing, and more importantly what they are choosing not to do? That would require an epic level of trust, which arguably the tech sector has never earned.

Although Amodei in his post proposed a three-point plan that included independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed, industry-wide regulation and global regulation, some observers question how this would work in practice.

"Nobody has given a substantive explanation of what 'slowdown' means," said Ed Zitron, CEO of EZ Primary Research.

"Putting a plant from METR, where one of the guys who quit Anthropic went, in every AI company? Democratic and global 'co-ordination'? Doesn't mean anything to me."

Zitron said stopping training AI models would leave them vulnerable to Chinese rivals.

"Their margins might improve but their products will be captured in amber and distilled by Chinese labs. They may have to change pricing. I truly don't know how it all works.

"This could burst the bubble. But right now we are very thin on what a 'slowdown' means."

In the UK, we have heard about plans to roll out the tech more widely within the NHS to improve patient care, and how AI gave the UK economy a much-needed boost over the summer. We are all being encouraged to use it more and more at work, in education and in our personal lives.
sources.headline: Questions mount over what an AI 'slowdown' would look like

stories.headline: Obama urges Democrats to make AI safety, jobs and regulation a central policy agenda

sources.body: Former President Barack Obama is urging Democrats — including 2028 presidential candidates and congressional leaders — to more aggressively focus on a comprehensive AI agenda, warning in a closed-door fundraiser that the technology is at an inflection point. “This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama said at the fundraiser Thursday, according to a partial transcript of his remarks provided by his office. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial.” Speaking alongside House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries at the New-York Historical Society in Manhattan, Obama said he is neither a “doomer” nor an “accelerationist.” His remarks come amid increasing alarm over the technology’s advance, with executives at two of the country’s leading AI labs joining Elon Musk in calling for slowing its development , following months and years of cries from within the industry for government to act. Obama said AI development would be “one of my central agendas” if he were running for president, throwing down a gauntlet as the shadow 2028 Democratic primary debate responded to the AI leaders’ calls. “I would have a very clear plan, and I would talk about this, and I would say, here’s our plan for safety, here’s our plan for making sure our kids are not corrupted by this,” Obama said, according to excerpts of his remarks shared with POLITICO by his office and first reported by The New York Times. Among the top concerns, Obama said: “I would be thinking about the economic impacts in very concrete ways and understanding what does it mean if there’s going to be job displacement. Where is that going to hit? How are we going to respond? Are there going to be limits to the amount of displacement that can take place? What is that going to mean for our social safety net? If it turns out that you’ve got a lot more people who can’t find full-time work because they’ve been rendered redundant, how are we going to respond?” He also called for Congress to take action, telling Jeffries that Democrats should “put together a framework for a very public conversation” centered on the biggest issues. Obama’s remarks mark a larger shift for both himself and the Democratic Party writ large: He governed as a tech-friendly Democrat, who broke POTUS tech barriers by having a laptop and iPad while in office and whose 2011 town hall at Facebook headquarters was widely seen as typifying the administration’s friendliness with Silicon Valley . The Obama era was also known for Washington’s failure to confront the growing monopolization of power in the tech industry, most famously in the Federal Trade Commission’s 2013 decision not to file an antitrust lawsuit against Google. (The first Trump Justice Department later filed such a suit seven years later.) Already on Sunday, at least two potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidates addressed the issue of slowing the pace of cutting-edge AI development, or otherwise keeping their products from launching pandemics or cyberattacks. Speaking on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said Democrats need to “address it head on.” “There needs to be safeguards. There need to be rules. There need to be limits. There needs to be a kill switch on rogue AI,” Buttigieg said, criticizing congressional Republicans and the White House for not moving quicker to rein in AI development. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, who has gone from courting AI investment to pumping the brakes on data center development, posted to X Sunday that it’s “long past time for our federal government to step up, take this seriously, and put up some guardrails — both here at home and on the global stage.” The calls for “some guardrails” are still much milder than the proposals coming from the far left of the Democratic caucus, including the proposal by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) to pause the development of advanced AI models and permanently ban “ artificial superintelligence .” And Obama’s remarks underscore the leadership vacuum in a Democratic Party that remains in the wilderness after brutal 2024 losses and continues to struggle to unify around a policy agenda. In a portion of his remarks, Obama acknowledged that challenge, saying that “part of the job for us is to give people a reason to believe again in the idea of the democratic project, the American project, the economy that works for everyone, opportunity for every kid, to reassure people that if we work together, we can deliver those things. That’s hard to do without somebody in the White House to lead the charge, but I do think that people are ready for that message.” President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has dismissed any worries about AI posing an existential threat, telling reporters last week that he’s mainly worried about beating China to dominate the technology. Obama compared AI to other “dangerous technologies like nuclear power,” but added that it did not have the same “natural” and "physical constraints” on it that is not “under state control.” In Congress, House and Senate lawmakers have sought to advance legislation to slow down or impose limits on AI development, so far without success. One key Senate proposal, led by Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) and Senate Majority Leader John Thune , faces an uncertain future because of differences over how to impose a legal duty on Silicon Valley companies that would hold them liable for harms their models cause. Another contentious issue is whether the legislation should preempt state from imposing their own AI laws. House Speaker Mike Johnson said Sunday morning he would support talks with tech leaders on AI but insisted that developers — not Congress — are primarily responsible for ensuring their products are safe. As lawmakers campaign in their districts ahead of the midterm elections, they are fighting to own the messaging as voters sour on data centers and the impact of AI systems on jobs and education, among other key areas.
sources.headline: Obama calls for Dems to focus on AI

stories.headline: Spain’s Ceuta migration crisis moves deeper into the courts

sources.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/L6V44OLWWNBOVD5EDKZFMXGZX4.jpg?auth=446f851dcb3b0c10a56eaf6a22b9b45add96369bd9e6c5794179b14b3fdb2baf" width="6526" height="4351" alt="Traslado de personas migrantes que dormían en la calle desde Loma Colmenar al nuevo emplazamiento del Gobierno en La Guardería (Ceuta)."></img><p>El Gobierno no ha entregado ninguna cabeza que pueda servir de cortafuegos ante las responsabilidades políticas por la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta. Ni tiene de momento la menor intención. La <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-11/dimite-el-jefe-de-gabinete-del-delegado-del-gobierno-en-ceuta-por-el-salto-fronterizo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-11/dimite-el-jefe-de-gabinete-del-delegado-del-gobierno-en-ceuta-por-el-salto-fronterizo.html">dimisión de Gonzalo Sanz</a>, jefe de gabinete del delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, es completamente ajena a La Moncloa. El <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-12/la-guerra-abierta-en-la-delegacion-de-ceuta-por-los-avisos-del-salto-fronterizo-atrapa-al-gobierno-en-un-nuevo-cruce-de-versiones.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-12/la-guerra-abierta-en-la-delegacion-de-ceuta-por-los-avisos-del-salto-fronterizo-atrapa-al-gobierno-en-un-nuevo-cruce-de-versiones.html">choque de versiones con su jefe</a> le ha llevado a alejarse de la Delegación del Gobierno y pensar en su propia defensa legal, ante la alta probabilidad de ser llamado a declarar por la Audiencia Nacional una vez que la jueza María Tardón ha decidido llevar adelante la instrucción. La judicialización de esta honda crisis va a condicionar la política, según reconocen interlocutores parlamentarios. El PP y Vox apuntan a que las investigaciones de los tribunales alcancen al Consejo de Ministros.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-14/el-salto-judicial-de-ceuta-condiciona-la-politica.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El salto judicial de Ceuta condiciona la política

sources.body:
El delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, ofrece una rueda de prensa con motivo del inicio del curso escolar en Ceuta, en la Delegación del Gobierno en Ceuta, a 9 de septiembre de 2026, en Ceuta (España). La vuelta a las aulas coincide / Marcos Moreno - Europa Press

La jueza María Tardón , que investiga en la Audiencia Nacional la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta ha reclamado reclama la investigación sobre el delegado del Gobierno abierta en Ceuta. En una resolución con fecha del pasado viernes, a la que ha tenido acceso EL PERIÓDICO, pide a su compañero del Juzgado número 6 de la Ciudad Autónoma que "valore la pertinencia de inhibirse de sus actuaciones" en su favor "si se tratase de conductas incluidas en el procedimiento" que ella ya está tramitando.

A principios de este mes, el juez número 6 de Ceuta abrió diligencias previas contra el delegado del Gobierno en esta ciudad, Miguel Ángel Pérez, tras la denuncia presentada por Manos Limpias -a la que se ha sumado Hazte Oír- sobre si supo por el CNI que podía ocurrir una avalancha y no actuó. Su jefe de gabinete dimitió la semana pasada tras inisistir en que trasladó los avisos.
sources.headline: La jueza que investiga la entrada masiva de inmigrantes reclama la investigación sobre el delegado del Gobierno abierta en Ceuta

sources.body:
La crisi de Ceuta són, en realitat, múltiples crisis. La més crua i urgent, la humanitària , després dels fets del 30 i 31 de juliol, quan més de 70.000 persones van saltar la frontera des del Marroc, per terra i per mar. Com a mínim 141 persones van morir ofegades. Encara avui, més d'un mes després, hi ha 2.000 nens i nenes identificats , esperant un futur que no arriba.

Darrere d'aquest moviment de persones, però, s'hi amaguen altres crisis: diplomàtiques, polítiques, econòmiques. Ceuta ha estat una peça més en la lluita d'interessos en el tauler global , que ha aprofundit en la desunió europea. L'episodi més cridaner va ser la reacció italiana de suspendre l'acord de Schengen amb Espanya per als viatgers no europeus.

El professor Javier Valencia , expert en ciberintel·ligència i assessor d'agències de seguretat estatals i internacionals, assegura al "30 minuts" "Ceuta, ciutat ostatge" de Montse Mora i Xavier Brichs, que el cas ceutí encaixa en el manual de l'anomenada guerra híbrida , en què les xarxes socials hi tenen un paper essencial.

Hi ha hagut desinformació, moviment migratori i aquesta imatge d'arribada exitosa s'ha reintroduït al canal per fer una crida encara més gran

Els atacs híbrids busquen objectius polítics utilitzant tot tipus d'eines –del sabotatge de cables submarins a la ingerència electoral– sense necessitat d'arribar a un conflicte armat. L'objectiu final pot ser forçar un canvi en la política exterior d'un altre país o desestabilitzar l'adversari.

Són campanyes amb un cost econòmic relativament baix i, sobretot, de difícil atribució. És a dir, no és fàcil assenyalar-ne un responsable directe . "En aquest cas, tot convergeix al Marroc. El problema és que molta gent vol una veure'n la prova definitiva i, en intel·ligència, moltes vegades aquest tipus de proves definitives d'atribució no les tenim mai", explica Valencia.

Pol Morillas, director del CIDOB , és del parer que "possiblement, per omissió hi ha una responsabilitat del Marroc en aquest control fronterer", mentre que el periodista Ignacio Cembrero, especialista en el Magreb , no té cap dubte que el paper de Rabat ha estat "fomentar i promoure sobre el terreny una entrada massiva d'immigrants". I apunta un possible per què.

El seu aparell de seguretat està molt disgustat amb la investigació de 14 mitjans sobre el funcionament dels serveis secrets, de la seva agència d'intel·ligència interior i de l'ús massiu que han fet de Pegasus

Els analistes subratllen que no es pot entendre el poder marroquí com un bloc monolític , sinó que cal diferenciar molt bé el cercle de poder que envolta la Corona, del govern i de la maquinària de seguretat de l'Estat.

Les eleccions legislatives del dia 23 poden donar claus per entendre les tensions internes en un país que, malgrat el control de la premsa, també està "traumatitzat", apunten els analistes, per tot el que ha passat. Els qui han tornat al seu país comparteixen com de malament ho han passat.

Els informes desclassificats pel govern espanyol evidencien que el Centre Nacional d'Intel·ligència (CNI) havia alertat sobre la campanya a les xarxes socials per assaltar la tanca, però que no en va calibrar la magnitud . El Marroc ha respost amb un llarg comunicat en què assegura que no hi ha "cap dada, fet o informe" que el vinculi a la crisi migratòria de Ceuta.
sources.headline: Ceuta, ostatge d'una guerra híbrida: "La instrumentalització de la migració anirà a més"

stories.headline: Spain’s electoral board considers how to implement the Supreme Court order on the Democratic Memory ‘grandchildren law’

sources.body: <p>La Junta Electoral Central (JEC) se reúne este lunes para estudiar<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-10/el-supremo-ve-en-la-ley-de-nietos-un-peligro-fundado-real-y-serio-de-afectar-a-las-elecciones.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-10/el-supremo-ve-en-la-ley-de-nietos-un-peligro-fundado-real-y-serio-de-afectar-a-las-elecciones.html"> los autos con los que el Tribunal Supremo</a> ha suspendido el derecho al voto de los nacionalizados por la <a href="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099">Ley de Memoria Democrática</a>, conocida como <i>ley de nietos</i>. La mayoría de los miembros de la JEC mantienen que no es su competencia discutir sobre el trasfondo de esa norma que permitió miles de nacionalizaciones de descendientes de exiliados por la Guerra Civil, que fue aprobada por el Gobierno y refrendada por el Parlamento hace cuatro años sin ser recurrida en sus plazos, y defienden que deben limitarse solo a resolver las dudas sobre cómo y en qué municipios deberían votar. Esa discusión ya se tuvo en su reunión de julio y se resolvió por nueve votos frente a cuatro. Los vocales propuestos por el PP defienden, en línea con la mayoría de la sala del Supremo, que la instrucción que flexibilizó las nacionalizaciones trasciende el contenido de la ley y que la JEC sí es competente.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-14/la-mayoria-de-la-junta-electoral-pretende-evitar-el-debate-sobre-la-decision-del-supremo-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: La Junta Electoral debate cómo dar cumplimiento a la orden del Supremo sobre la ‘ley de nietos’

sources.body:
El ministro para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública, Óscar López, ha calificado de "salvajada" y "atropello democrático" la decisión del Tribunal Supremo de suspender cautelarmente la 'ley de nietos' , que preveía dar la nacionalidad a los descendientes de los exiliados de los españoles.

En una entrevista en La Hora de La 1, López ha asegurado que, aunque en España hay "cientos de jueces" que se esfuerzan porque la justicia sea "justa" e "independiente", también hay otros "sectores judiciales" que, en su opinión, "se empeñan en tumbar al Gobierno" y "que son salvapatrias".

Y ha culpado de ello al PP, y en concreto al expresidente del Gobierno José María Aznar, por decir que "'el que pueda hacer, que haga'". En su opinión , la derecha vive "rendida", y acomplejada" y solo "copia" los discursos e insultos de la "ultraderecha" , y está todo el día alimentando la teoría de la conspiración, diciendo que lo que busca el Gobierno con esta ley es alterar el censo de cara a las próximas elecciones, al dar el derecho al voto a los nuevos nacionalizados.

Sin embargo, ha subrayado que en las elecciones generales de 2023, el PP fue el principal beneficiado de esa ley, porque el voto exterior hizo que el PSOE perdiera un escaño en Madrid, que fue a parar al PP.

Asimismo ha reprochado al PP que digan que su objetivo es defender a España, pero ha remarcado que "defender España es crecer tres-cuatro veces que lo que crece Alemania" o "subir las pensiones, llenando la hucha" o que a España se la vea con "orgullo" por ser "un país que más se ha opuesto a la guerra en Gaza o Irán", o que esté "a la vanguardia contra el cambio climático".

Un día más, el Gobierno ha insistido en que nadie previó la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta de los pasados 30 y 31 de julio. El ministro ha reiterado que no había informaciones que llevaran "a constatar que se iba a producir un asalto de 70.000 personas". "¿Que hay amenazas permanentes y alertas permanentes? Claro que sí. ¿De esa dimensión? No", ha zanjado López, para advertir después que "afirmar lo contrario es verdaderamente irresponsable".

Y ha confiado en que no se vuelva a producir un hecho similar, que ha calificado de "desconocido y extraño", y ha pedido "tranquilidad y plena confianza". En este punto, ha defendido que "España tiene unos grandes servicios de seguridad, tiene unos grandes servicios de Defensa y de Interior".

Asimismo ha sostenido que España tiene capacidad para defender sus fronteras, al tiempo que se respeta la "legtalidad internacional y los derechos humanos". En este punto se ha preguntado que qué habrían hecho el PP y Vox de tener una crisis así y se ha mostrado convencido de que habría sido "un verdadero desastre".

También ha vuelto a cuestionar a la jefa de la Audiencia Nacional María Tardón, que investiga la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta, por pedirle a los polícias que no informaran a sus superiores, pero que después se filtrara ese informe a un medio de comunicación 24 horas antes de la comparecencia de Sánchez. "Cada día creo menos en las casualidades, sobre todo cuando hay esa coincidencia en los tiempos", ha subrayado.

stories.headline: Justice Minister Félix Bolaños challenges the judiciary over its dismissal of his complaint against Judge Peinado

sources.body: <p>El ministro de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, Félix Bolaños, sigue adelante con su determinación de que no quede sin sanción la actuación del juez Juan Carlos Peinado. Bolaños presentó entre marzo de 2025 y abril de 2026 ante el Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) —el órgano competente para sancionar a los jueces— una serie de quejas por distintos comportamientos del magistrado que van desde el polémico interrogatorio que Peinado le hizo en el despacho del ministro hasta el intento de imputación de Bolaños rechazado de plano por el Supremo, pasando por la limitación del papel de la Fiscalía en la causa o la filtración de escritos a la prensa antes de que se notifiquen a las partes. Después de 427 días desde la primera queja, el responsable de la acción disciplinaria de los jueces decidió no sancionar a Peinado<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/las-19-quejas-de-bolanos-sobre-peinado-que-el-cgpj-archivo-censuro-mi-expresion-facial-y-me-prohibio-sonreir.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/las-19-quejas-de-bolanos-sobre-peinado-que-el-cgpj-archivo-censuro-mi-expresion-facial-y-me-prohibio-sonreir.html">, según la resolución notificada el mes de </a>agosto, porque entendía que todo forma parte de la actuación jurisdiccional. El titular de Justicia ha presentado el último recurso en esa vía, acusando al Poder Judicial de “corporativismo” y de ser “incapaz” de “reponer” la “reputación” del órgano, y ha anunciado su intención de llevar el asunto hasta el Tribunal Supremo. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-14/duro-reproche-de-bolanos-al-poder-judicial-por-no-sancionar-a-peinado-le-acusa-de-corporativismo-y-de-danar-la-reputacion-de-la-justicia.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Duro reproche de Bolaños al Poder Judicial por no sancionar a Peinado: le acusa de “corporativismo” y de dañar la reputación de la justicia

sources.body:
El ministro de Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, Félix Bolaños , ha cargado duramente contra el Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) por su "corporativismo" y "conservadurismo" y ha recurrido su decisión de archivar las quejas que él mismo emitió contra las "irregularidades" del juez Juan Carlos Peinado, instructor de la causa contra Begoña Gómez.

El ministro ha denunciado ante el Poder Judicial en varias ocasiones presuntas irregularidades del Juez Peinado, la primera el 4 de junio de 2025.

Entre ellas, se ha referido a la supuesta "extralimitación" en sus funciones cuando tomó declaración a Bolaños como testigo y cuando pidió al Supremo que le investigara por malversación y falso testimonio. Una petición que desestimó el alto tribunal por falta de indicios.

Bolaños también denunció presuntas filtraciones de escritos a la prensa antes de que se notificaran a las partes, entre otras cuestiones.

En un escrito dirigido a la Comisión Permanente del órgano de gobierno de los jueces, al que ha tenido acceso RTVE, Bolaños carga contra su falta de "agilidad, rigor y defensa del interés general".

"Las irregularidades denunciadas protagonizadas por el magistrado instructor, muchas de ellas ampliamente conocidas por la opinión pública, han hecho un daño notorio e irreparable al buen nombre de la Justicia" , expone Bolaños.

Y añade: "Lamentablemente, el CGPJ ha sido incapaz, bien por conservadurismo, bien por corporativismo, de corregirlas y reponer así el prestigio y la reputación del Poder Judicial, evidentemente dañado por la instrucción protagonizada por el denunciado, también en mi declaración testifical".

Bolaños denuncia una "vulneración de sus derechos fundamentales" por no haberle permitido acceder a las diligencias sobre el juez Peinado.

Y justifica su recurso "no porque confíe en que la Comisión Permanente del CGPJ vaya a revocar su propia decisión", sino porque dice tener la "convicción" de que la Sala Tercera del Tribunal Supremo "hará el trabajo que correspondía al CGPJ: defender y proteger el buen nombre de la judicatura".

El Poder Judicial resolvió en agosto que no procedía sancionar a Peinado al entender que esto no formaba parte de la actuación jurisdiccional.

Al respecto, el titular de Justicia denuncia que los hechos denunciados " no han recibido la respuesta jurídica que cabía esperar del órgano al que constitucional y legalmente se encomienda el ejercicio de la potestad disciplinaria sobre jueces y magistrados".

En este sentido, recalca que, desde que presentó su primer escrito de queja, han transcurrido 427 días , pese a que la investigación se circunscribía a "actuaciones muy concretas, perfectamente identificadas y de muy sencilla comprobación". Y denuncia que durante este tiempo la actividad instructora desplegada ha sido "francamente limitada , habiéndose practicado un número muy reducido de diligencias de investigación".

El ministro recuerda que en todo este tiempo se solicitó "hasta en tres ocasiones" que se agilizaran las diligencias y recuerda que la Constitución atribuye al Consejo "funciones en materia de inspección y régimen disciplinario" ( poder sancionar a un magistrado ).

stories.headline: Macron will make a state visit to Spain on September 29 and 30

sources.body: <p>El presidente de Francia, <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/emmanuel-macron/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/emmanuel-macron/">Emmanuel Macron</a>, visitará España los próximos 29 y 30 de septiembre, según han anunciado este lunes La Moncloa y El Elíseo ―la residencia oficial del presidente de la República Francesa― en un comunicado conjunto. “La visita de Estado se desarrolla en el marco de las relaciones de amistad y cooperación que mantienen ambos países y del trabajo que realizan para seguir reforzando la relación bilateral en todos los ámbitos”, recoge el comunicado.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-14/macron-visitara-espana-el-29-y-30-de-septiembre.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Macron visita España en la recta final de su mandato y en pleno bloqueo del acuerdo de cooperación entre ambos países

sources.body:
El presidente de la República Francesa Emmanuel Macron visitará a España los días 29 y 30 de septiembre, en un viaje oficial en el que se reunirá con el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez . Fuentes de Moncloa y del Elíseo acaban de anunciarlo de forma conjunta en dos difundidos de forma simultánea en el que señalan que Sánchez y Macron mantendrán una cita bilateral en la sede de la presidencia del Gobierno a mediodía del 30.

El viaje del presidente de la república francesa a España se celebra, según fuentes de Moncloa, "en el marco de las relaciones de amistad y cooperación que mantienen ambos países y del trabajo que realizan para seguir reforzando la relación bilateral en todos los ámbitos".

“ 🔴 Moncloa confirma que el presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, realizará una visita de Estado a España el 29 y 30 de septiembre para seguir reforzando la cooperación entre ambos países ▪️ La última vez que Macron visitó España fue en 2023 con motivo de la cumbre… pic.twitter.com/h0vkflnsth “

La visita llega en plena crisis migratoria en Ceuta . Macron trasladó a Sánchez su "solidaridad" y ofreció ayuda a España a través de la Agencia Europea de Guarda de Costas y Fronteras (Frontex). El dirigente francés no se sumó a las críticas a España encabezadas por Italia, que pidió su expulsión del espacio de libre circulación europeo conocido como 'Schengen' y estableció controles temporales a viajeros.

La última vez que Sánchez y Macron se encontraron frente a frente fue el pasado mes de julio, cuando el presidente español viajó a París para asistir al desfile de la fiesta nacional francesa y a la reunión de la llamada Coalición de Voluntarios". Fue una reunión de trabajo que se celebró con el objetivo de reforzar los acuerdos conseguidos en las cumbres de la OTAN y del G7 sobre el apoyo a Ucrania.

Sánchez y Macron se veían por primera vez tras la polémica columna de opinión escrita por expresidente Mariano Rajoy , que en los días previos al mundial de fútbol hablaba de una selección francesa "sin franceses". El Gobierno francés criticó las palabras del expresidente del Gobierno al que calificó de "racista".

A su llegada a los Campos Elíseos, donde se celebró el desfile, Sánchez se disculpó por esas palabras ente el primer ministro francés Lecornu y la primera dama: "Estoy tan avergonzado", dijo el presidente.

El presidente francés viajará a España acompañado de su mujer, Brigitte Macron . Ambos serán recibidos por los reyes, que ofrecerán en su honor una cena de gala.

La cita se producirá ocho años después del viaje oficial de Felipe y Letizia a París, en octubre de 2018. Desde entonces estaba pendiente esta visita que se ha ido posponiendo por varios motivos, incluida la imposibilidad de ratificar definitivamente el Tratado de Amistad .

Sánchez y Macron sellaron este pacto durante la última visita del francés a nuestro país, en enero de 2023. Sin embargo la polémica en torno al artículo 2.4, en el que se prevé que un ministro pueda participar en el Consejo de Ministros del otro, al menos una vez cada tres meses y por rotación, ha impedido hasta la fecha su ratificación.

stories.headline: Barcelona rental listing draws nearly 2,000 applications in an hour, highlighting the housing crunch

sources.body: Aconseguir un pis de lloguer de tres habitacions a Barcelona per 1.000 € al mes i amb un contracte per cinc anys de durada actualment és un fet noticiable i “una loteria”. Així ho ha viscut el Joaquim Pujolar i la Selén Dikmen, una parella jove que va signar el contracte el 31 d’agost. El propietari del pis els va dir que l’anunci de lloguer a internet, que van retirar-lo en menys d’una hora, va rebre fins a 1.800 sol·licituds . El que no sabien els “afortunats” és que l’ API que es va fer càrrec de la intermediació a través del portal Idealista no els havia de cobrar absolutament res per la gestió o el canvi de nom dels subministraments del pis, però va demanar-los 242 € . “Ara és obligatori que ho assumeixi el propietari i no hi ha cap manera de fer trampes, qui faci això estarà fent un frau”, afirma la Montse Bassas , vicepresidenta del Col·legi d’Administradors de Finques de Barcelona-Lleida . També et pot interessar Collboni celebra la llei europea d’habitatge: “Avança en el camí que Barcelona ha emprès” Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura IA per filtrar les sol·licituds de lloguer L’oferta i la demanda de pisos de lloguer a Barcelona és tan extremament desigual que per cada pis que es posa al mercat, els administradors de finques, els API o els propietaris reben una quantitat de sol·licituds inassolible per poder revisar. És per això que hi ha professionals del sector que fan servir la intel·ligència artificial per seleccionar els millors candidats. Ho explica a betevé la Montse Bassas, que està al capdavant de Basmi Finques. En el cas d’aquesta parella, quan van veure el pis a internet van enviar una sol·licitud a l’ API que gestionava l’oferta i també van insistir moltíssim amb trucades fins que van poder parlar amb ella i així concertar la visita del pis. També et pot interessar PIMEC alerta que la crisi de l’habitatge ja està afectant la competitivitat de les empreses Cristina Brotons 3 minuts de lectura Els propietaris volen llogaters amb bons ingressos El fet que els propietaris puguin escollir entre centenars de candidats també els dona el poder de filar molt prim sobre el perfil que creuen que més els encaixa. Segons el Col·legi d’Administradors de Finques de Barcelona-Lleida , el que busquen els propietaris bàsicament és solvència però també estabilitat , és a dir, volen llogaters que paguin cada mes i no marxin, que finalitzin els contractes signats per no haver de buscar-ne d’altres. El Joaquim i la Selén van presentar les nòmines , la vida laboral, una carta de presentació i també van afegir una carta de recomanació de l’antiga propietària del pis on estaven. El Joaquim assegura que en altres ocasions els havien arribat a demanar fins i tot l’extracte bancari. “Et demanen molts requeriments abans d’aconseguir la visita”, afirma. També et pot interessar El calvari dels estudiants per trobar pis: “Alguns deixen la carrera perquè no ho poden assumir” Núria Granados 3 minuts de lectura Diversitat d’interpretacions sobre drets i deures Actualment els administradors de finques i els API no poden cobrar als llogaters les despeses de gestió d’un contracte de lloguer residencial, tot i que segueix passant, però on no hi ha una norma única es sobre qui ha de pagar l’ IBI o les despeses de comunitat . En el cas d’aquesta parella se’ls ha cobrat les dues quantitats. Paguen un contracte de lloguer de 911 € , 391 € d’ IBI anuals i 56,98 € mensuals de despeses de comunitat , així que acaben pagant mensualment 1.000,62 € pel pis. Segons la Montse Bassas, vicepresidenta del Col·legi d’Administradors de Finques de Barcelona-Lleida , hi ha “massa normativa” i reclama a les administracions canvis realistes per dinamitzar el mercat de lloguer. “Corregir allà on ens hem equivocat”. Posa d’exemple el fet que segons el seu parer, i el col·legi que representa, “mai s’hauria de considerar com a gran tenidor un propietari de cinc habitatges “. També et pot interessar El govern prorroga un any més la declaració de zona de mercat residencial tensionat Cristina Brotons 2 minuts de lectura

stories.headline: Residents displaced by the L9 sinkhole prepare a collective lawsuit as Catalonia plans a permanent support office

sources.body: Ja han passat més de dos mesos des que es va produir l’esvoranc de l’L9 , que va obligar desallotjar 300 veïns i comerciants del barri de Sant Gervasi – la Bonanova . Després de tot aquest temps, encara hi ha 18 famílies desallotjades i les causes de l’incident continuen sent una incògnita . Aquesta situació genera malestar entre els veïns i, per això, aquest dilluns mateix presentaran una demanda a la Generalitat i a l’Ajuntament . Per això el govern català obrirà una oficina d’atenció permanent per a tots els afectats de les obres . També et pot interessar Malsons, incertesa i por: així viuen els veïns de Sant Gervasi un mes després de l’esvoranc Lola Santiago 3 minuts de lectura Així ho ha explicat la delegada de la Generalitat a Barcelona , Pilar Díaz, al Bon dia, Barcelona . Díaz ha apuntat que aquesta oficina servirà per acompanyar els veïns que “se sentin preocupats”, així com per resoldre els dubtes que puguin tenir. L’oficina estarà operativa fins que finalitzin les obres de l’L9, tot i que encara no hi ha data d’obertura . Ara per ara, els veïns tenen un punt d’informació per manifestar les seves preguntes o malestar. “Els protocols no devien estar tan apamats” Díaz també ha explicat que el govern continua investigant les causes de l’incident, perquè no es torni a repetir el mateix i per reforçar els protocols de seguretat , els quals “semblava que estaven molt estudiats i apamats, però ara resulta que no ho devien estar tant”. Malgrat aquesta revisió, la delegada ha insistit que l’obra era segura . De fet, ha apuntat que abans de fer treballs com aquest, es col·loquen sensors a la zona per determinar si hi ha canvis en el terreny. En el cas de Sant Gervasi, diu, aquests sensors van detectar moviments abans que els veïns alertessin de l’esvoranc . També et pot interessar Col·legi de Geòlegs, sobre els dos esvorancs i l’explosió: “Barcelona té una geologia complexa” Helena Molist Sancho 1 minut de lectura “L’Administració ha de respondre” Els afectats per l’esvoranc presentaran aquest dilluns, 14 de setembre, una demanda col·lectiva contra la Generalitat i l’Ajuntament . La delegada del govern ha confessat que ho entén: “Només faltaria, aquestes persones s’han trobat en una situació que no han provocat elles mateixes, per això l’Administració ha de respondre “. Ara bé, també ha volgut deixar clar que un cop es determinin les causes de l’esvoranc, “ l’Administració també reclamarà el que li pertoqui “. També et pot interessar Paneque apunta que la causa de l’esvoranc de l’L9 podria ser la manca de formigó en una cavitat Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura Recupera l’entrevista
sources.headline: La Generalitat obrirà una oficina d’atenció permanent per als afectats de les obres de l’L9

sources.body:
Veïns i comerciants afectats per l'esvoranc de l'L9 a Sant Gervasi, a Barcelona, presenten aquesta setmana una demanda col·lectiva contra la Generalitat de Catalunya . Així ho ha anunciat aquest dilluns l'advocada que representa els afectats, Carmen Pérez-Pozo Toledano, en declaracions a "Els matins": "Reclamarem danys materials, danys econòmics i danys morals".

Per la lletrada, la Generalitat ha fallat en el seu deure de vigilar que les obres es fessin correctament, un supòsit que en dret s'anomena "culpa in vigilando". "Quan contractes algú perquè faci una feina has de vigilar que la faci bé, i això no ha passat. Si no, no tindríem l'esvoranc", explica.

"Presentarem una demanda col·lectiva en què reclamarem danys materials, econòmics i morals." Els afectats per l'esvoranc de l'L9 es querellaran pels fets d'ara fa dos mesos. Ho explica @CristinaMBlanch , que ha parlat amb veïns https://t.co/pWYyxHV4ls #Matins3Cat pic.twitter.com/NbrUQaSL5F

La demanda es presentarà, així, dos mesos després de l'aparició del sot de grans dimensions, quan encara hi ha desallotjats els veïns de 33 habitatges i 8 locals comercials . Mentre que, d'aquests, 15 podran tornar a casa en un termini d'unes cinc setmanes, als veïns de 18 habitatges i 7 negocis , situats als carrers Rubinstein, 2 i 4, i de Teodora Lamadrid, 3, se'ls allargarà la situació com a mínim fins al gener.

"M'han trencat la vida, jo tenia una vida molt tranquil·la. Horrible. Una sensació de no tenir casa...", diu a TV3 la Maria Teresa, una de les veïnes afectades.

En la mateixa situació està la Miren, que, com la majoria dels altres desallotjats, des del 7 de juliol dorm en un hotel amb la resta de la seva família. "No són allotjaments adequats. No són sostenibles en el temps. No es pot tenir una família separada en dues habitacions", explica a Catalunya Ràdio.

En aquesta cara de la moneda també hi són els comerços. Els botiguers de la zona qualifiquen l'esvoranc de "ruïna" i denuncien la manca d'ajudes de les administracions, que només els ofereixen la possibilitat de rebre crèdits .

"Les nostres nòmines, com a autònoms, no les assumeixen. Només els lloguers i factures posteriors a l'esvoranc: de factures en tenim poques, després del sot poques compres hem fet, tenint en compte que hem hagut de tancar", explica a 3CatInfo Cristina Ayza, propietària d'una botiga de roba i bijuteria. Com altres comerciants, la Cristina ha hagut de romandre tancada la major part de l'estiu i s'ha vist obligada a posar a la venda tots els productes a preus molt rebaixats.

"Jo no vull un crèdit, vull solucions", diu per la seva banda Katherine Sánchez, que regenta una joieria. En el seu cas, a més, tampoc podrà fer la campanya de Nadal, ja que no podrà reobrir fins al gener.

Més positiu és el propietari de la pizzeria Verona, on es va localitzar l'esvoranc. "De mica en mica anem fent. L'Institut Català de Finances i l'Ajuntament ens estan ajudant. Es van pagant les factures de mica en mica. Temps al temps", ha explicat a Catalunya Ràdio Domingo Finez.

stories.headline: Rodalies launches a new app with real-time train tracking and service information

sources.body: (ACN) Rodalies té una nova aplicació mòbil que permet consultar informació en temps real sobre l’estat del servei ferroviari , seguir la ubicació dels trens , comprar bitllets en línia i accedir a mapes interactius, entre d’altres usos. L’app, impulsada per Renfe, incorpora la intel·ligència artificial per facilitar la cerca de rutes i rebre contingut personalitzat segons els hàbits de mobilitat de cada usuari. Aquesta nova aplicació substitueix l’actual plataforma de Rodalies , que deixa de funcionar aquest 15 de setembre . També et pot interessar Renfe permetrà viatjar amb gossos de fins a 40 quilos a partir del 21 de juliol Cristina Brotons 2 minuts de lectura Millores en accessibilitat La plataforma també permet fer cerques per veu i guardar trajectes preferits, a més d’oferir millores en matèria d’accessibilitat per garantir una experiència inclusiva per a tots els usuaris. La nova app compta amb un disseny visual que reforça la marca Rodalies, tant a través dels colors corporatius com dels elements gràfics que l’identifiquen. La consellera de Territori, Habitatge i Transició Ecològica, Sílvia Paneque , afirma que la nova eina “combina una imatge pròpia amb les funcionalitats més avançades per oferir als usuaris una experiència moderna , intuïtiva i adaptada a la realitat del territori”.
